Reports To: Human Resources Manager

About Pacific Health Group

At Pacific Health Group, we care deeply about the people and communities we serve. We meet individuals with kindness, respect, and understandingâlistening first, honoring each person's journey, and offering support without judgment.

Through compassionate, person-centered healthcare, behavioral health services, and social supports, we walk alongside people as they work toward healing, stability, and a healthier, more hopeful life.

Our Core Values

  • Speak with integrityâclear, respectful, and honest in every interaction
  • Embrace innovation, trying new ideas, learning fast, and improving care.
  • Own our roles, staying accountable for outcomes and documenting accurately
  • Build genuine connections with members, families, and teammates through empathy and cultural sensitivity
  • Lead with trust by being consistent, transparent, and following through
  • Celebrate wins together, recognizing individual and team achievements
  • Collaborate with purpose, partnering across departments and with community providers to solve problems
  • Ask for support and offer support, because thriving together is how we serve our members best

Role Overview & Impact

The Human Resources Coordinator provides administrative and operational support across the Human Resources department. This entry-level position supports onboarding, employee records, HR system transactions, recruitment coordination, employee communications, and general HR department operations.

The HR Coordinator serves as an initial point of contact for routine employee and applicant questions and ensures that requests are directed to the appropriate HR team member. The successful candidate will be highly organized, service-oriented, comfortable using technology, and committed to maintaining the confidentiality and accuracy of employee information.

Key Responsibilities

Core Responsibilities

Recruitment & Talent Coordination

  • Support candidate communications using approved templates
  • Track candidate status and documentation in the applicant tracking system
  • Assist with pre-employment requirements
  • Maintain accurate recruiting records and candidate files
  • Support job fairs, community outreach, internship activities, and recruiting events
  • Provide a professional, timely, and welcoming candidate experience

Onboarding & Offboarding

  • Coordinate pre-employment and onboarding activities after an offer has been accepted
  • Send new-hire forms, instructions, orientation schedules, and required notices
  • Track completion of pre-employment requirements, background checks, employment documents, and onboarding tasks
  • Coordinate the timely completion and retention of Form I-9 documentation in accordance with established procedures
  • Coordinate with hiring managers, Payroll, Information Technology, Learning and Development, and other departments to support new-hire readiness
  • Confirm that new employees receive appropriate system access, equipment information, schedules, and introductory materials
  • Support new-hire orientation logistics and attendance tracking
  • Follow up on incomplete forms or onboarding requirements
  • Initiate separation checklists after receiving appropriate authorization
  • Schedule exit interviews or distribute exit questionnaires

HR Compliance & Documentation

  • Assist with personnel-file, I-9, benefits, training, and HR data audits
  • Track required documents, acknowledgments, certifications, and renewal dates
  • Assist with preparing records for internal and external audits
  • Follow established HR policies, procedures, record-retention requirements, and confidentiality standards
  • Escalate incomplete, inconsistent, or potentially noncompliant documentation
  • Maintain current versions of approved HR forms, templates, notices, and resources
  • Support the distribution and tracking of required employee notices

Benefits & Employee Support

  • Route plan interpretation and eligibility questions to the HR Generalist or appropriate team member
  • Support annual Open Enrollment communications, scheduling, and administrative preparation
  • Assist with routine employee reminders and documentation follow-up
  • Maintain confidentiality of medical and benefits information
  • Support benefits and leave audits as requested

HR Operations & Administrative Support

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourself

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • You've grown a team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup

  • Managed tech leads or a second manager

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 45 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

We're hiring the third designer because there's more good work to do than two people can handle — and we'd rather ship faster than slow down.


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to European market leadership.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of product design work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.

What we believe

Compliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm.

Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work.

What the role is

We expect strong design skills, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end.

Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster:

  • Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast.

  • Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked.

  • Build the tools and skills — Cursor rules, design QA skills, prompt templates — that let engineers do good design work without you in the room.

The leverage is doing all four well. Doing only one is the wrong shape.

How we work

  • No PMs. Designers and engineers run product. You talk to customers, frame the problem, write the spec, decide what ships.

  • Small temporary teams. You plus one or two engineers per project. Whoever is closest to the problem leads.

  • Design leads the logic; engineering tests feasibility. You bring the V1. Engineers push back on what's expensive or risky, and start ahead with system design. They help spot edge cases. You adjust it fast. We get from v1 to v4 in a matter of hours or a few days.

  • Prototype-grade, not wireframes. Real components, real states, real copy. Sometimes an LLM-built prototype before Figma. The component library stays current because the speed of design depends on it.

  • Handoff is the beginning, not the end. You're in the engineering channel. You review the PR. You verify on production. Staging QA is the first gate, not the last.

  • In-sync culture with a thoughtful comms mindset. Loom for reviews, Notion for specs, quick loops in Gather where written comms don’t cut it, all happening in the same time zone. Teammates are reviewing things quickly. Engineers and designers spend under two hours in weekly meetings.

  • AI is part of the craft. We use Claude to pressure-test ideas, draft specs, surface edge cases, and write test cases. Not to skip thinking.

The first three months

  • Month 1. Ship your first design to production. Get into the codebase, the customer language, the way we write specs. Sit on customer calls.

  • Month 2. Own a full feature end-to-end. Customer conversations, problem framing, Figma, spec, engineer pairing, PR review, production verification.

  • Month 3 and beyond. Push the design system forward. Start building the tools and skills that make engineers faster at design. Improve the product design process. The bar is yours to defend.

Who you are

  • 8+ years designing B2B SaaS desktop applications as Staff/Principal Product Designer or similar. Dense interfaces — tables, filters, permissions, settings pages.

  • You've been the only designer, or one of two or three, in companies under 50 people at least once before. You know how to set the bar without a design org behind you.

  • Your portfolio is "I," not "we." You can name the engineer you paired with on each feature, the design decision you defended through the build, and what happened when the feature reached users.

  • You communicate clearly and concisely in English: in Slack, in docs and on a call.

  • You're fast in Figma with or without AI. You’re already in a serious relationship with LLMs.

  • You treat engineering feasibility as input, not a constraint. When an engineer says "three weeks, here's why," you find the version that's 80% as good and ships next week.

  • You're comfortable doing product work without the PM title.

  • You hear feedback and come back the next day with something better. You don't spend the hour in between defending the version that's already outdated.

Compensation

Salary + equity based on experience. The offered compensation depends on the individual's qualifications assessed during the interview process.

What we offer

Interview process

We aim to invite you to a first conversation within a week and give feedback after every stage.

  • Intro call with talent team (~45 min)

Order may flex depending on availability. If you make it to the exercise and don't get an offer, we'll tell you specifically what got in the way.

Learn more at taktile.com.

  • At least 3 years of professional full-stack software engineering experience, with experience delivering moderately complex projects or features.

  • Experience in React

  • Good communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • The ability to work in a hybrid model from our Berlin HQ, the London office, or the Iasi hub. Please note that relocation assistance is not provided for this role.

Ideal, But Not Required

  • Familiarity with system design concepts and architectural trade-offs

title: Senior Communications Specialist (Global Communications)
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Help shape how one of Europe's most ambitious deep-tech companies is understood by the world.

  • As a member of the Communications team, you will lead the execution of our global communications workstream, translating company priorities into high-impact media engagement, executive positioning and integrated campaigns—ensuring the right stories reach the right audiences at the right time.

  • Use communications to help secure financing, build trust, shape public debate and make one of the world's most ambitious engineering projects visible long before its impact becomes obvious.

  • Own communications around Proxima's defining moments—from engineering breakthroughs to strategic partnerships and political milestones.

  • Pair strategic judgement with exceptional execution, identifying the stories that matter and bringing them to life with creativity, precision and impact.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Global Media Relations

  • Own Proxima's day-to-day media engagement in Germany and internationally.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all media enquiries and manage these with speed and sound judgement, ensuring responses are accurate, consistent and aligned with Proxima’s broader positioning.

  • Build trusted relationships with journalists across business, technology, science and political media across our key markets

  • Create high-impact media opportunities around Proxima's biggest moments through proactive pitching, interviews, briefings and lab tours.

Corporate communications and thought leadership

  • Develop interview briefings, opinion pieces and executive messaging that position Proxima's leadership among the leading voices shaping the future of fusion, industrial innovation and European technology.

  • Translate complex technical, commercial and political topics into compelling narratives for investors, policymakers, industry partners, future talent and the public, ensuring every communication reinforces Proxima's strategic positioning.

  • Stay close to the political, policy and industry landscape, identifying opportunities where strategic communications can shape public debate, strengthen Proxima's credibility and advance the company's commercial and policy objectives.

  • Proactively identify story angles, campaign ideas and emerging communications opportunities that help Proxima lead the conversation around fusion, industrial innovation and Europe's energy future.

Strategic campaigns and external engagements

  • Turn communications priorities into integrated campaigns with clear narratives, audiences, channels, timelines and measurable outcomes

  • Lead public relations for selected international conferences, sponsorships, exhibitions and executive speaking engagements—from opportunity assessment and messaging to content and delivery.

Cross-functional Collaboration & Program Delivery

  • Build trusted relationships across Engineering, Finance, Public Policy, and Business Operations.

  • working closely with colleagues across Communications and Brand & Content to deliver integrated communications programs.

  • Lead external agencies and specialist partners, ensuring consistently high standards across every aspect of delivery.

WHO YOU ARE

Must-haves

  • 8+ years of experience in corporate communications, media relations, public relations or strategic communications, ideally across agencies and high-growth technology companies or startup to scale-up environments.

  • A strong network of or the credibility to quickly build trusted relationships with German and international journalists across business, technology and science media.

  • A track record of leading integrated communications campaigns from strategy through execution, including managing agencies and external partners.

  • Native or fluent German, with exceptional writing and communication skills, in both German and English.

  • A strong understanding of how strategic communications can shape public debate, influence policy conversations and support business objectives.

  • An entrepreneurial mindset with the initiative to identify opportunities, take ownership and drive communications forward in a fast-moving environment.

  • Exceptional organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple high-profile priorities simultaneously.

Nice to have

  • Experience in deep tech, energy or another highly technical, highly regulated industry.

  • Experience in political or policy communications

  • Experience supporting fundraising or investor communications.

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

  • Design real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

YOUR IMPACT

As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you will significantly contribute to the design, analysis, validation and realisation of Proxima’s Alpha stellarator fusion machine. Your innovative and detailed engineering work will deliver robust mechanical, structural, and thermal performance of critical systems, tooling and manufacturing processes. You will also work with external collaborators and suppliers to develop the designs, equipment, systems and materials that will enable Proxima’s mission to deliver clean, sustainable fusion energy.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Develop innovative solutions and detailed mechanical designs for significant systems within the Alpha stellarator, ensuring integration with the broader physics, mechanical and structural systems.

  • Carry out thermal and structural analysis and assessment of mechanical designs, providing design input and implementing recommended design improvements.

  • Conduct technology trade-offs, materials selections and feasibility studies to facilitate the successful identification of the Alpha net energy stellarator.

  • Design, deliver, and support the prototyping and verification of the components, materials, assemblies and manufacturing processes selected for Alpha.

  • Work with external suppliers and collaborators to assist and guide the development and manufacture of the components and systems that will come together to demonstrate the net energy Alpha stellarator.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • High performers with excellent communication and problem-solving skills who love challenges and are not afraid to experiment, take risks, and learn from mistakes.

  • Experience in designing and analysing mechanical components and assemblies, with proficiency in CAD (experience with 3DExperience/CATIA v6 and ANSYS is highly beneficial, but not essential).

  • Experience in designing and delivering the conceptual and detailed design of mechanical, structural, thermal or electro-mechanical equipment, particularly for use in research, development, prototyping and manufacturing.

  • Knowledge and experience of designing and selecting materials for some or all of the following engineering applications: high temperature, cryogenic, electromagnetic, vacuum.

  • Demonstrated ability to work with and manage external suppliers, with multidisciplinary technical teams in fast-paced, dynamic settings.

  • Proficiency with programming languages used in science and engineering (particularly Python) is highly beneficial but not essential.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-45 min)

  • Portfolio Presentation & Review (45-60 min)

  • Technical Panel Interviews (2x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

Successful applicants will be assigned to one of the Engineering teams within Proxima, depending on their specific skills, location, and the needs of the organisation.

This role sits at L2/L3/L4 of our framework, please inquire during the recruitment process for further information

We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Most of what makes an AI solution survive contact with a large enterprise is not the AI. It is the engineering discipline around it, and that discipline is what you bring. You do not need to arrive as an AI expert - you arrive as someone who knows how professional software gets built, shipped, and kept alive, and you grow into the agentic side alongside a team that is already deep in it.   • Shaping how we develop: issue workflows, branching and review standards, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, security checks, and release management

  • Deep working knowledge of the professional software development lifecycle: issue tracking and workflows (e.g. Jira), code review and development standards, CI/CD, automated testing, security scanning, versioning and releases

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung als Product Owner, Product Manager oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle, idealerweise in einem B2B-SaaS-, Plattform- oder Marketplace-Umfeld.

title: Principal Brand Designer (Spain or Portugal - based role)
description:
About the Role

At OLX, Design is more than aesthetics, it's how millions of people build trust, discover opportunities, and connect with their communities. As Principal Brand Designer, you'll shape how OLX and its portfolio of brands are experienced across every customer touchpoint.

Reporting to the Director of Product Design, you'll define the visual principles, creative systems, and brand standards that unite a diverse portfolio while allowing each brand to express its unique identity. This is a highly strategic, hands-on individual contributor role for someone who combines exceptional craft with systems thinking, influences through expertise, and embraces AI as a catalyst for creativity, consistency, and scale.

Working in close partnership with Marketing, Brand Strategy, Product Design, Communications, Employer Brand and regional teams, you'll translate business strategy, customer insights and brand positioning into cohesive creative systems that strengthen brand equity, build customer trust and accelerate high-quality execution across the organisation.

You'll establish the creative vision and quality bar for brand design, while building the frameworks, governance and tools that enable teams worldwide to create distinctive, consistent and impactful brand experiences.


What you'll own

Define the future of OLX’s  Group's brand ecosystem

Partnering with the Director of Product Design, Marketing and Brand Strategy, you'll evolve the visual identity and creative direction across OLX Group and its portfolio of brands. You'll ensure our brands feel connected where they should, distinctive where they need to be, and consistently recognisable across every customer touchpoint.

  • Group-wide brand identity systems and visual standards

  • Brand visual identity governance, quality assurance and design principles

  • Multi-brand design systems and asset libraries

  • Creative direction across digital, physical and experiential touchpoints related to brand design (excludes advertising)

  • Long-term evolution of OLX Group's visual identity and assets.

    • Build scalable creative systems powered by AI

    You'll help define how AI enhances brand design across OLX Group by developing AI-ready design systems, prompt libraries, reusable templates, automation workflows and governance that empower teams to produce high-quality work consistently and efficiently.

    Rather than replacing creativity, you'll ensure AI amplifies craftsmanship, accelerates production and strengthens consistency while maintaining the integrity of every brand.

    You'll also stay ahead of emerging technologies, identifying opportunities where AI can improve creative workflows, collaboration and design quality across the organisation.

    Raise the creative standard across OLX Group

    As the most senior brand design practitioner, you'll establish the benchmark for the application of brand design across  product launches, executive communications, presentations, employer branding, events, web experiences and marketing initiatives.

    You'll provide creative direction, thoughtful critique and hands-on design leadership, ensuring every expression of the brand reflects exceptional craft, clarity and purpose.

    Translate strategy into brand experiences

    You'll partner closely with Marketing and Brand Strategy from the earliest stages of initiatives, transforming customer insights, research and business priorities into compelling visual systems and brand experiences.

    You'll contribute strategic thinking—not simply execute briefs, helping teams solve complex business challenges through design that strengthens trust, recognition and long-term brand value.

    Drive adoption and influence across the organisation

    Creating great systems is only part of the role, you'll ensure they're embraced.

    You'll build documentation, enablement programmes, design resources and governance models that help global and regional teams confidently apply OLX Group's brand standards.

    You'll influence senior stakeholders across Product, Marketing and Executive Leadership, aligning teams around a shared creative vision and ensuring design has a meaningful voice in strategic decision-making.

    Mentor and elevate the craft

    As a Principal Designer, your influence extends well beyond your own work.

    You'll coach designers through critique, mentoring and collaboration, fostering a culture of craftsmanship, systems thinking and continuous improvement. While this isn't a people management role, you'll be recognised as a trusted design leader whose expertise elevates the entire organisation.


    What we're looking for

    We're looking for a strategic design leader with exceptional craft, systems thinking and a passion for building brands that scale globally.

    You create brands that people trust 

    Your portfolio demonstrates outstanding work across visual identity, typography, layout, storytelling, motion and digital experiences. You understand how to create memorable brands—and how to evolve and steward them over time.

    You think in systems

    You build frameworks, governance models, templates and design systems that enable organisations to produce consistently exceptional work. You know that the best design creates lasting capability, not just individual deliverables.

    You bring strategy to life through Design 

    You're comfortable partnering with Marketing, Brand Strategy and executive stakeholders, translating positioning, customer insights and business objectives into creative systems that deliver measurable business impact.

    You're fluent in AI-enabled Design

    You already incorporate AI into your creative practice and understand where emerging technologies create value, and where human judgement remains essential.
    You can translate those insights into scalable workflows that improve quality, speed, experimentation and consistency across teams.

    You influence without authority

    You communicate with clarity, build trusted relationships and bring people together around a shared creative vision. You're equally comfortable presenting to executives, collaborating with marketers or mentoring fellow designers.

    You bring depth of experience

    You'll likely have:

  • 10+ years of experience in brand design, or visual design

  • Experience building or evolving brands at scale across multiple products or markets

  • Expertise in Figma and/or Adobe Creative Suite

  • Experience with motion design, storytelling, and digital brand experiences

  • Experience building or contributing to enterprise design systems

  • Deep familiarity with AI-powered creative tools and workflows

  • Outstanding communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills


    • Why join OLX

    OLX operates some of the world's most recognized online marketplaces, connecting millions of people every day to buy, sell, find jobs, discover homes, and build businesses.

    As our Principal Brand Designer, you'll have a unique opportunity to shape the future of multiple global brands while defining how AI and design systems work together to create consistent, high-quality brand experiences at scale.

    This role offers the chance to influence design beyond individual projects to build the frameworks, standards, and creative vision that will guide OLX's brands for years to come.

    If you're excited by solving complex brand challenges, setting the highest creative standards, and pioneering the future of AI-enabled design, we'd love to hear from you.


    Hiring Process
    We believe in a transparent and collaborative hiring process that reflects how we work as a team. Here’s what you can expect:
     
    First Stage 
    Portfolio & Design Leadership 
    This is a 90-minute session with the Hiring Manager. We’ll dive deep into your portfolio to assess your design craft, strategic thinking, systems mindset, and collaboration skills. This is also an opportunity to showcase your leadership in design and discuss how you approach complex challenges.

    Second Stage 
    Multi-Brand Systems & Creative Leadership 
    In this 60-minute session, you’ll meet with a senior leader from the Creative team. We’ll explore your ability to build, evolve, and govern brand systems across a complex multi-brand organization. This stage focuses on your creative leadership and how you ensure consistency and innovation across diverse brands.

    Third Stage 
    Executive Partnership & Business Impact 
    This 45-minute session is with a senior leader from the Marketing team. We’ll assess your leadership presence, ability to form strategic partnerships with Marketing, and your commercial thinking. This is also a chance to discuss how you drive organizational influence and deliver business impact through brand design.

    Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at OLX
    OLX values diversity and welcomes applicants of all races, ethnicities, disabilities, ages, genders, sexual orientations, religions, backgrounds, and experiences to apply. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet all the requirements - you may be just the right fit for this or other opportunities with us!
     
    Data Process Policy
     
    OLX will process your personal data to assess your fit for the applied position. You may optionally consent to store your data for up to 12 months after the application process for consideration in future OLX roles. For more details on how your application data will be processed please check our Privacy Statement.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About us

Join bonify, Germany’s leading platform for credit scoring and financial management. We are on the mission to revolutionize the FinTech industry and make the credit score and financial data available and transparent for our users.

We are hiring a Senior Product Designer to shape how millions of users understand and improve their financial health across mobile and web.

You'll own design end-to-end for a defined product area, from framing the right problems through research, prototyping, validation, and delivery. Our focus is on creating more value beyond the credit score, making complex financial information feel simple, useful, and trustworthy, and embedding AI into both our products and our daily work.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role with a strong research mindset. You'll speak directly with German-speaking users, work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data, contribute to our design system, and support less experienced designers through collaboration and feedback.

Your tasks

  • Lead product design for a defined area across mobile and web.
  • Turn complex financial and credit-related information into experiences that feel simple, useful and trustworthy.
  • Plan and conduct customer research, interviews and usability testing, particularly with German-speaking users.
  • Translate qualitative research and behavioural data into clear product decisions.
  • Create user flows, interaction models, prototypes and polished product experiences in Figma.
  • Work closely with Engineering to ensure solutions are feasible, scalable and implemented with high quality.
  • Partner with Product and Data to define what success looks like and evaluate the impact of shipped work.
  • Contribute to and improve reusable patterns and our design system.
  • Use AI practically in your day-to-day work to accelerate research, exploration, prototyping and documentation.
  • Help shape AI-powered customer experiences where relevant — while applying strong judgement around trust, clarity and user control.
  • Share your expertise, give thoughtful feedback and help raise the quality of design across the team.

Requirements

  • You have around 6–8 years of experience in product design, ideally working on digital consumer products.
  • Strong experience designing end-to-end product experiences across mobile and web.
  • Advanced skills in Figma, interaction design and prototyping.
  • Strong hands-on user research experience — not only consuming research, but planning and conducting it yourself.
  • The ability to simplify complex, data-heavy or sensitive topics into clear customer experiences.
  • Strong product thinking and the ability to connect design decisions to customer and business outcomes.
  • Experience working closely with Product, Engineering and Data in cross-functional teams.
  • Confidence working independently and taking ownership from ambiguity through delivery.
  • German at C1 level or above, including the ability to conduct customer interviews and usability studies.
  • Strong practical experience using AI tools in your design workflow — for example in exploration, synthesis, prototyping or documentation.
  • A collaborative, kind and constructive working style.
  • Experience in fintech, banking, financial services or another regulated/data-intensive environment is a strong plus.

What we offer

As part of the bonify team, you'll have:

  • The opportunity to take ownership from day one
  • The chance to thrive in a dynamic and flexible startup environment.
  • Access to extensive coaching and training programs through our personal development budget
  • 30 vacation days
  • Subsidies for BVG and UrbanSportsClub
  • 1:1 language classes in both German and English.

The Company is committed to the principle that no employee or job applicant shall receive unfavourable treatment on grounds of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy, and maternity.

Please note, to be compliant with AML Offices, due to the specifics of fintech industries additional background checks are required (applicable only at the offer stage).

If you're ready to make a meaningful impact in the world of FinTech and embark on an exciting career journey, apply now to join bonify!

You will work closely with the Industrialization team and our external consulting partners, taking responsibility for clearly defined work packages in documentation, data management, and production planning preparation.

You will collaborate across Production, Engineering, Quality, and Logistics, gaining first-hand experience of a real production ramp-up from the very beginning and seeing how a prototype-based setup evolves into a scalable and repeatable serial production process.


What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Support the shopfloor planning activities at our Göppingen site by documenting current-state processes and contributing to layout planning, material flow design, and production cycle data (e.g., cycle times, workstation utilization, and walking distances).

  • Support process design activities by helping to structure and document assembly processes for different vehicle variants down to individual work-step level.

  • Create and maintain illustrated work instructions for production processes.

  • Collect, prepare, and analyze process-related data using Excel.

  • Support qualification and training activities by maintaining workstation-specific skill matrices and preparing training materials for assembly teams.

  • Prepare and follow up on workshops and alignment meetings with external consulting partners, including meeting minutes, task tracking, and status reporting.



What you bring to the team:

  • You are currently pursuing a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Logistics, or a comparable field of study.

  • You are proficient in using Excel and PowerPoint; initial experience with CAD or layout planning tools is a plus.

  • First practical experience in manufacturing, workshop environments, or through academic projects is welcome, but not required.

  • You work accurately and reliably when creating documentation and maintaining data, including recurring tasks.

  • You have a structured and independent way of working and are willing to take ownership of your tasks and follow up on topics proactively.

  • You communicate openly and professionally and enjoy collaborating with colleagues from Production, Engineering, and external partners.

  • You are available to work regularly on-site in Göppingen; the scope and duration of your engagement can be tailored individually.

  • You have good German and English language skills.

  • You have experience using AI tools effectively.

  • You are available to start immediately or by November 1st at the latest.

Why Quantum-Systems:

Wir glauben an die Stärke kombinierter Fähigkeiten: klare technische Expertise gepaart mit einer kundenorientierten Ausrichtung. Wir sind Branchenpioniere, die ehrgeizig, mutig und visionär sind. Wir überschreiten Grenzen, blicken über den Tellerrand und streben nach technologischer Exzellenz, um die Zukunft unbemannter Systeme mitzugestalten. Wir versprechen, dass wir Deine Startbahn für individuelles und berufliches Wachstum sein werden.

Our benefits:

  • Flexible working hours: With our trust-based working time model, you have the flexibility to manage not only your working hours but also your work-life balance independently.

  • Stay active: Through the EGYM Wellpass, you gain access to thousands of fitness and sports facilities, and we subsidize your membership.

  • Corporate Benefits: Take advantage of attractive offers and discounts from well-known brands and providers such as Adidas, Apple, and Expedia.

  • Team Events: We believe in growing together and celebrating our successes as a team.

About us:

Quantum Systems specialises in the development, design, and production of small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS). The company’s range of electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) sUAS are built to maximize range and versatility and to provide operators with a seamless user experience. By integrating cutting-edge software capabilities, like edge computing and real-time AI-powered data processing, Quantum Systems is building next-generation UAS for clients in defence, security, public sectors.

Our commitment:

We are an open-minded company that not only values diversity, but actively promotes it. Regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation or disability, we firmly believe that the diversity of our employees is an essential part of our success.

At our company, every voice is heard and every perspective is valued. We believe that our differences enrich us and help us to find creative solutions and generate innovative ideas. We pride ourselves on creating an inclusive work environment where all employees can reach their full potential.

description:
Warehouse Associate

Location: Hoxton (E2)

Working pattern: Onsite | Part-time | Shift-based (15 hours per week)

Pay: £14.40 per hour

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Site Operations team powers the physical side of our marketplace through HOP (our rapid grocery delivery service) and Editions (our network of delivery-only kitchens). From launching new sites to ensuring operational excellence across markets, we combine retail and hospitality expertise with operational rigour. If you thrive in hands-on environments and want to help redefine how food and groceries reach customers—come join us on the ground.

We’re looking for a Warehouse Associate to join our Hoxton team. Our Warehouse Associates are the beating heart of our day-to-day site operations. You’ll work closely with your management team to ensure our loyal customers get what they want when they need it, ensuring the smooth running of our Hop sites.

Get to know our Site Operations team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

What You’ll Be Doing

Here’s what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Execute precise order fulfillment by picking customer essentials quickly and accurately to meet delivery deadlines.

  • Maintain product integrity by ensuring all goods received and dispatched meet our high standards for freshness and quality.

  • Facilitate seamless logistics through clear communication with riders to ensure prompt order handovers.

  • Drive inventory excellence by supporting the intake of daily stock deliveries and assisting with ongoing inventory management.

  • Champion site safety and standards by maintaining a clean, organized warehouse environment for the whole team.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

  • Adaptability in fast-paced environments, with the ability to remain focused under pressure.

  • Strong attention to detail to ensure order accuracy and high-quality stock control.

  • Effective communication skills to collaborate with teammates, managers, and riders.

  • A proactive, hands-on mentality with a drive to solve problems as they arise on-site.

  • A customer-first mindset, understanding that your speed and accuracy directly impact the user experience.

  • Previous experience in FMCG, Retail, or Warehouse environments is valued but not required.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, operations are central to how we build trust across our marketplace. You’ll work in a fast-paced environment where service excellence drives real impact.

  • 🔧 See the impact of your work in real time: Solve problems as they happen, turning challenges into positive experiences across our three-sided marketplace.

  • 🌱 Grow through doing: Develop problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills with structured progression pathways and real opportunities to move into management.

  • 🤝 Be part of a tight-knit culture: Work collaboratively to achieve shared goals in an environment that values support, ownership, and resilience.

  • 🕒 Flexibility that works for you: Enjoy the benefits of shift-based work that fits your schedule.

Our Interview Process

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine:

  • Step 1: Apply – Apply for any role you’d like to be considered for. We’re looking forward to hearing from you.

  • Step 2: Online assessment – If your application is successful, you’ll receive an assessment from our AI hiring assistant, Maki People. Please note: this must be completed to continue.

  • Step 3: Initial conversation – One of our Recruitment team will get in touch to talk through your experience and what you’re looking for next.

  • Step 4: Final Onsite interview – You’ll be invited to an onsite interview with one of our Site Managers.

  • Step 5: Outcome – We’ll get back to you quickly after your interview to let you know the result!

Our Global Structure

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

title: Vendor Manager
description:
Role Profile

 

About Radiant

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure - from powered land, to compute, to software .

As we scale our platform and expand our engineering organisation, we are looking for leaders who can build strong teams, uphold high standards, and deliver reliably at pace.

 

About the Infrastructure Team

The Infrastructure Team spearheads the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of critical HPC/AI infrastructure to the broader Technology and Customer organizations. Its mission is to deploy scalable, secure, and efficient infrastructure solutions tailored to the organization's strategic needs. The team defines Radiant's supercomputers' reference architecture in line with the customer, software, and operational requirements of the company.

They work closely with third-party suppliers to provide and maintain the list of technologies that form part of Radiant's portfolio of offerings. Because that portfolio is built almost entirely on external capacity — GPU cloud providers, OEMs, colocation and datacenter partners, networking and storage vendors — the strength of Radiant's supplier relationships is inseparable from the strength of its platform.

 

Vendor management sits at the centre of that. The Vendor Manager owns how suppliers enter Radiant's ecosystem, what commercial terms we hold them to, and whether they perform against those terms once deployed. They partner with the broader Radiant team to turn a fragmented supplier base into a governed, tiered portfolio the delivery teams can rely on.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own the vendor onboarding process end to end, taking new suppliers through a tiered model that matches the depth of diligence to the depth of the relationship:

    • Known vendor: transactional suppliers. Entity and sanctions screening, financial viability, security questionnaire, standard terms, payment setup.

    • Partner: recurring or material spend. Deeper due diligence, named commercial and technical owners on both sides, negotiated terms, defined SLAs, and an agreed review cadence.

    • Strategic partner: suppliers Radiant depends on for capacity, continuity, or roadmap. Executive sponsorship, joint QBRs, capacity and roadmap alignment, exit and continuity planning, and concentration-risk review.

  • Run intake triage for new supplier requests: assign the right tier, drive the diligence to completion, and keep the pipeline moving so delivery teams are not blocked waiting on process.

  • Maintain a single source of truth for every infrastructure and compute contract — terms, renewal and notice dates, committed spend, reserved capacity, price escalators, and termination rights.

  • Run renewals on a forward calendar rather than as a fire drill, flagging every material renewal ahead of its notice window with a recommendation to renew, renegotiate, or exit, backed by usage data.

  • Ensure compliance requirements flow into commercial terms before and during negotiations

  • Track consumption against commitments and flag under-utilised reservations or approaching overage before they hit the budget, feeding real usage patterns back into the next negotiation.

  • Define and report the KPIs and SLAs that matter, such as allocation against reservation, incident frequency, provisioning lead times, support responsiveness, and invoice accuracy.

  • Run the vendor review cadence: monthly or quarterly reviews for partners, and QBRs with executive attendance for strategic partners.

  • Own escalation and remediation when a vendor underperforms — raise it, document it, agree a corrective action plan, and pursue service credits where they are earned.

  • Establish vendor incident notification requirements & playbooks (timeframe, escalation, documentation) for breach response and incident communication.

  • Maintain a vendor scorecard that Infrastructure leadership can read in five minutes and take to the executive team.

  • Own third-party risk assessment and periodic re-assessment across security, data protection, financial, and geographic or concentration risk, in partnership with Security and Legal.

  • Keep certifications, insurance, and data-protection documentation current (SOC 2, ISO 27001, DPAs, sub-processor disclosures), and support internal and customer audits with clean, retrievable vendor records.

  • Maintain continuity and exit plans for single-source dependencies, so that for any critical supplier Radiant knows what the fallback is and roughly what switching would cost in time and money.

  • Support the establishment of vendor management best practices and continuously improve the process, templates, and documentation through the participation of "lessons learned" workshops.

 

Requirements

  • BSc in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years in vendor management, IT procurement, strategic sourcing, or supplier operations, with meaningful time spent on technology and infrastructure categories.

  • Demonstrated experience managing infrastructure and compute suppliers, such as GPU providers, OEMs, networking or storage vendors.

  • Proven track record negotiating and managing complex technology contracts, including MSAs, SOWs, DPAs, SLAs, and multi-year committed-spend agreements.

  • Fluency with the commercial mechanics of compute: committed use and reserved capacity, rate cards, burst and overage pricing, egress and transfer costs, SLA credit structures, renewal escalators, and liability caps.

  • Sufficient technical literacy to hold a credible conversation with infrastructure engineers about GPU, networking, and storage, and to distinguish a genuine capacity constraint from a negotiating position.

  • Experience designing and operating vendor governance frameworks — tiering, onboarding, due diligence, performance scorecards, and third-party risk assessment.

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a track record interfacing with various types of stakeholders (engineering/operations teams, vendors, legal, finance) and writing clear deliverables.

  • Comfortable working in fast-moving, high-complexity technical environments, and building process where none currently exists.

 

Nice to have

  • Prior work experience in HPC, hyperscale, Telco, or AI infrastructure environments involving large-scale compute procurement.

  • Working knowledge of the GPU and AI hardware vendor landscape (NVIDIA and its OEM channel, alternative accelerator vendors, neocloud providers) and how their allocation models and roadmaps work in practice.

  • Understanding of datacenter commercial models, including colocation agreements, power contracts, and capacity reservation structures.

  • Familiarity with vendor management or contract lifecycle management (CLM) tooling, and with procurement workflows in ERP systems.

  • Exposure to export controls, sanctions screening, or hardware supply-chain constraints affecting GPU and networking availability.

  • Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits from the third-party risk side.

  • A professional procurement or contract management qualification (CIPS, WorldCC, or equivalent).

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Wave is now the largest financial institution in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire, with millions of users, growing rapidly year-on-year. And, we're still in the early days of our product roadmap and potential impact on people's everyday lives.

We're looking for an engineer who's independent and excited about getting things done. You'll be responsible for building and improving the ways people pay with Wave. You'll own every step of the process: from understanding the problem to shipping your solution to users to helping the customer support team resolve problems.

You'll join an autonomous, cross-functional team focused on a single area of Wave's product. Each team is led by a Product Manager and an Engineering Manager or Tech Lead. We organize projects to give you as much ownership as possible. Typically, you'll be responsible for a feature or improvement end-to-end, from design through deployment.

Our to-do list changes constantly, but here are some recent projects:

  • Enabling people to use their Wave app to pay for products in stores.
  • Allowing people to pay their electricity bills with Wave by integrating with electrical utility companies.
  • Building an app for business owners to pay their employees' salaries using Wave.
  • Allowing people to pay for their transportation on taxis, trains & buses.

Our stack:

  • backend: Python 3 (+ mypy)
  • API layer: GraphQL
  • android frontend: Kotlin/Jetpack
  • iOS frontend: Swift/SwiftUI
  • web frontend: TypeScript/React
  • database: Postgres/CockroachDB
  • infrastructure: GCP/Terraform
  • orchestration: Kubernetes

We expect all engineers to be willing to work across the entire stack, including mobile. Prior experience in these technologies is a strong plus, but not required.

Key Details

  • This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso.
  • Wave provides a yearly $1,200 stipend to support coworking meetups with teammates.
  • Remote team members are expected to travel to our operational markets (e.g. Senegal or Côte d'Ivoire) at least once a year. Exceptions apply, but we've found this key to understanding our users and product.
  • Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary of up to $152,100 USD, plus a generous equity package.
  • Major benefits:
    • Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country).
    • 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance.
    • Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days exclusive of statutory holidays.
    • $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 5 years of professional experience as a product engineer.
  • Fluent in English, (bilingual in French is a big bonus!)
  • Successful candidates must be willing to travel to one of our operating locations at least once per year for a minimum of 6 consecutive days.

You might be a good fit if you

  • Reflexively ask yourself, "is this code the best way to make my users happy?"
  • Want to learn to solve hard problems and aren't afraid to ask for help when you get stuck.
  • Are excited to learn about complex systems.
  • Can communicate clearly with colleagues who work, speak and think differently.
  • Work to make things easier for the next engineer who will touch your code.
  • Always try to improve as a programmer and colleague.
  • Are excited to deeply understand the inner workings of the tools you use.

About engineering at Wave

We care about the big picture. We don't hire engineers to just ship tickets. We hire them to solve problems. That means caring deeply about outcomes, understanding context, and jumping in wherever something's broken, even if it's technically "not your area." When we see problems, inefficiencies, or opportunities to make something better, we act. We dig into operational issues, clarify fuzzy product specs, or step into unfamiliar code to help unblock teammates.

We move as fast as possible. Speed matters. It lets us try things quickly, get feedback early, and course-correct while it's cheap. So we write small PRs. We aim for MVPs. We leave TODOs and file follow-ups. We don't over-perfect v1. That said, we're building a financial product. Some things—like money movement, correctness, or security—deserve more caution.

We like boring technology. We favor tools that are reliable, well-understood, and easy to debug. This keeps us focused on solving meaningful problems instead of wrestling with unpredictable infrastructure. If a new technology helps us move faster, build safer, or solve a real need, we'll consider it. But we don't adopt tools just because they're new—we adopt them because they're right.

Simplicity is a strategy. It lets us focus our energy where it matters most: serving our users.

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

  • You will maintain accurate records of all requests, decisions, and rationale to ensure full auditability
